svg.title: Figure 3
svg.desc: Figure 3. How well the sky for each latitude and sidereal time fits the disc. Left: projection centre free. Right: zenith fixed at the centre of the disc, a reading of Law 5.700/1971. Darker is a better fit (lower rms). Grey: at least one of the 27 stars is below the horizon. Plus sign: Rio de Janeiro (the 23° S cell) at 12 sidereal hours. Circle: the best cell.

rdf:Description.dc:creator: Rodrigo Jazinski
rdf:Description.dc:source: Jazinski, R. (2026). Composed, not observed: What the celestial disc of the Brazilian flag carries of the sky over Rio de Janeiro on 15 November 1889, and what its texts supply (Working paper, version 0.0.7). Zenodo. https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.24480292

svg.text: Zenith fixed at the disc centre
best fit → twice the best rms
Plus sign: Rio de Janeiro, 12 sidereal hours. Circle: best cell. Grid 1° × 15 min. Data: flagsky_inverse_v0_0_7.csv.
